facts.fact: An APC and AZUR Développement survey of police stations in Pointe-Noire and Nkayi, run December 2013 to January 2014, states that work in the commissariats is manual at almost every level, that the few computers found there serve only for secretarial work, and that there is no digital archiving.

The APC and AZUR Développement survey (December 2013 to January 2014) states that Nkayi's commissariats hold one or two computers each on average, used by two to four self-taught officers for typing, scanning and printing documents, with the work otherwise manual and no internet connection at the station.

The APC and AZUR Développement survey (December 2013 to January 2014) names no station in its area of Pointe-Noire and Nkayi making a digital record: Nkayi has eight police posts besides the central commissariat and one gendarmerie brigade, and the survey says the commissariats' computers serve secretarial work only.
